title: Qualify skill activation descriptions with fal.ai
body:
The descriptions of fal-platform and fal-realtime in skills/claude.ai use service-independent phrases such as "check usage" and "Realtime". Those phrases can match requests about unrelated services.

Suggested descriptions:
- fal-platform: Manage fal.ai model pricing, usage, API credentials, and cost estimates.
- fal-realtime: Build and troubleshoot real-time image generation with fal.ai models.

Keep detailed model coverage and examples in the body. For routing checks, "check my Codex usage" should not select fal-platform, while "check my fal.ai usage" should. A generic real-time audio request should not automatically select fal-realtime.

title: README: add "Built on genmedia" section for third-party skills
body:
genmedia is becoming an execution layer for skills outside this repo, and the README has no place that shows that. This adds a small **Built on genmedia** section for third-party skills, seeded with one production example.

**[HyperShots](https://github.com/hypersocialinc/hypershots)** (MIT) generates App Store screenshots from a coding agent — deterministic HTML rendered at exact store dimensions with a fail-closed spec validator — and uses **genmedia as its generative layer**: GPT Image 2 + BiRefNet for transparent sticker art, and image-to-image style passes with a re-composite step that keeps the output store-compliant. Its references document verified genmedia API behaviors (upload `cdn_url`, `image_urls` array literals, `image_size` objects, one skill per `genmedia skills install`), and its install flow offers to install genmedia + the fal-models-catalog skill when missing.

Every image on [hypershots.dev](https://hypershots.dev) — including the site's own icons — was generated through genmedia.

Disclosure: I'm the author of HyperShots. If you'd rather track ecosystem links elsewhere (or not at all), happy to close — or adapt this to whatever format you prefer.

title: fix(fal-workflow): quote multiline description so YAML frontmatter parses
body:
## Problem

`npx skills add fal-ai-community/skills --skill fal-workflow` fails with:

```
■  No matching skills found for: fal-workflow
●  Available skills:  (16 listed — fal-workflow missing)
```

even though `skills/fal-workflow/SKILL.md` exists and is in `index.json`.

## Root cause

The `description` in `skills/fal-workflow/SKILL.md` is an **unquoted (plain) YAML scalar** containing `Two modes: ` (a colon followed by a space) and inline double quotes:

```yaml
description: Author and execute multi-step media pipelines on fal.ai. Two modes: (A) declarative ...
```

In YAML, `: ` is the key/value indicator, so a strict parser treats `Two modes:` as a nested mapping key and throws `bad indentation of a mapping entry` (reproduced with `js-yaml`, error located on the `description` line).

- `scripts/build-skills-index.py` uses a lenient regex parser, so the skill still landed in `index.json`.
- But `npx skills add` parses `SKILL.md` with a **strict** YAML parser (js-yaml), which throws and the CLI **silently skips** the skill → 16 of 17 skills found.

## Fix

Convert the description to a **folded block scalar (`>-`)** — the same style `genmedia-workflow` already uses and that `build-skills-index.py` supports — so `:` and `"` become literal and both parsers accept it. Regenerated `index.json` via `scripts/build-skills-index.py` (only the `fal-workflow/SKILL.md` sha256/bytes change).

## Verification

```bash
python3 scripts/build-skills-index.py --check   # → index.json is up to date
npx skills add fal-ai-community/skills --skill fal-workflow   # now resolves
```

title: genmedia: teach agents about smart routing and auto-category filtering
body:
## Summary

The genmedia CLI gained smart-default routing and auto-category inference in [fal-ai-community/genmedia-cli#8](https://github.com/fal-ai-community/genmedia-cli/pull/8). Until SKILL.md teaches this, agents keep their old habit of picking endpoints themselves and bypass the routing entirely — verified empirically: a Claude Code session running `genmedia run "a cat in a hat"` picked an explicit endpoint based on this skill's "Critical rules" rather than letting the CLI route.

This PR updates the skill content so agents prefer smart routing for default-quality requests, with explicit endpoint discovery still available when the user names a model or needs non-default behavior.

## Changes

### `skills/genmedia/SKILL.md`

- **Critical rule #2 added**: prefer smart routing for default-quality requests. The "Never invent endpoint IDs" rule drops to #3 with refined guidance for the explicit path.
- **Critical rule #4 (schema) clarified**: smart routing only needs `prompt`; schema inspection is required for explicit endpoints with custom params, not for default routing.
- **Quick patterns reordered**: smart routing leads (`genmedia run "a cat on the moon"`), explicit-endpoint demoted to a later section. New smart-routing async + poll example shows how to extract `endpoint_id` from the response for follow-up `status` calls.
- **Discover section** mentions `--no-classify` and that `genmedia models` auto-applies `--category` from the same classifier.

### `skills/genmedia/references/full-reference.md`

- Split the `run` section into "Smart routing (preferred)" and "Explicit endpoint" with a sample `routed` JSON block and the three `source` values (`manifest` / `cached` / `baked-in`).
- Added `--no-classify` to the `models` flag table and a paragraph on auto-category inference.

### `skills/index.json`

Regenerated via `scripts/build-skills-index.py` — sha256 + bytes updated for both files.

## Why this matters

Smart routing as a CLI feature is necessary but not sufficient. Agents do whatever the skill tells them. Without this update, the new ergonomics ship in the binary but agents still go through the discovery dance because the skill content tells them to.

After this PR lands and gets pulled into installed projects via `genmedia skills update genmedia`:

- `genmedia run "a cat"` becomes the canonical pattern in agent reasoning, not an alternative.
- Default token cost per generation drops from 3-4 LLM turns (read 50+ endpoints, pick one, fetch schema, run) to one shell call.
- `genmedia models "<query>"` returns a focused list (~10 entries scoped to the inferred modality) instead of 50+ across all modalities — direct context-savings for the agent.

## Test plan

- [x] Built `skills/index.json` via `python3 scripts/build-skills-index.py` — clean output, 16 skills, byte/sha changes only on `genmedia/SKILL.md` and `genmedia/references/full-reference.md`.
- [x] Visual review of the rendered SKILL.md and full-reference.md.
- [x] Manual smoke once landed: in a real Claude Code session with this skill installed (via `genmedia init` or `genmedia skills update genmedia`), prompt `"Generate a quick logo"` and verify the agent uses `genmedia run "<prompt>"` (no endpoint) instead of running discovery first.

## Cross-links

- CLI side: [fal-ai-community/genmedia-cli#8](https://github.com/fal-ai-community/genmedia-cli/pull/8) — the implementation that this skill update teaches agents to use.

title: Restructure repo around genmedia CLI: foundational, umbrellas, verticals
body:
## Summary

Architectural overhaul aligned with the [genmedia CLI](https://github.com/fal-ai-community/genmedia-cli) as runtime. Repo now follows a three-tier hierarchy (Skill, Reference, Section). Skills are knowledge layers, not API wrappers.

## New structure

**Foundational (1)**
- `genmedia`: full CLI surface (models, schema, run, status, upload, pricing, docs)

**Umbrellas (3)**
- `fal-models-catalog`: 10 modality references with curated endpoint picks (text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, text-to-3d, image-to-3d, text-to-audio, audio-to-text, image-to-text). About 250 endpoints curated from a hand triage of fal.ai's full 1,326-endpoint catalog into ~50 use-case buckets.
- `fal-prompting`: family-specific guides (Kling, GPT Image 2, Happy Horse).
- `fal-recipes`: 10 use-case pipelines (cinematography, character-design, commercial, storytelling, character-lipsync, image-restoration, virtual-tryon, video-with-audio, product-shot, realism).

**Verticals (5)**
- `fal-workflow`: now two modes. Mode A authors workflow JSON for the fal.ai cloud runtime; Mode B drives the genmedia CLI for local orchestration. Mode B integrates the genmedia-workflow content (pipeline-patterns, node-rules, utility-endpoints, recipes).
- `fal-gamedev`: 2D pixel-art game assets (added).
- `fal-train`, `fal-redesign`, `fal-regenerate-3d`: preserved.

## Other changes

- Imported source skills from upstream PRs (cinematography, character-design, commercial, storytelling, model-routing, genmedia-workflow). Their content is also consolidated into the umbrella references for the canonical agent path.
- Each umbrella and vertical has a Runtime note pointing at the genmedia skill.
- Cross-skill markdown link paths fixed to use sibling-relative form (`../skill-name/...`).
- Stripped em-dashes, smart quotes, and non-English remnants from agent-facing content (intentional French TTS demos preserved as multi-language showcase).
- Regenerated all 28 distribution `.zip` packages.
- All 28 `SKILL.md` frontmatter files validated: `name` matches folder name, descriptions are explicit triggers.
- Older single-endpoint skills (`fal-3d`, `fal-audio`, `fal-image-edit`, `fal-upscale`, etc.) are preserved for backward compatibility; their knowledge has been consolidated into the umbrella skills above.

## Test plan

- [x] 28 SKILL.md frontmatter validates (name = folder)
- [x] 76 internal markdown links resolve
- [x] 28 folder ↔ zip 1:1 match, no junk in zips
- [x] 0 em-dashes, smart quotes, or unintended non-English content
- [x] All scripts retain executable bits
- [ ] Reviewer to spot-check a few catalog picks against latest fal.ai endpoint availability
- [ ] Reviewer to confirm no breaking changes for users of legacy `fal-*` skills

fal-redesign: strip trailing content after </html>
body:
## Summary

When opus-4.7 writes the final HTML + tile-prompt JSON, it sometimes runs past the token budget and spills a trailing ```` ```tiles ```` code fence (or other commentary) **after** the closing `</html>` tag. That trailing text renders as visible body content in the browser and leaks the internal tile spec into the final page.

This PR truncates the HTML at `</html>` during `cleanupHtml()` so anything after the document end is silently discarded.

## Repro

Run `implement` on a content-heavy page (e.g. a full dashboard with inventory + stats + activity feed). Opus occasionally closes `</html>` then keeps writing:

```html
</body>
</html>

```tiles
{ "tiles": [ { "file": "tile-01.jpg", ... } ] }
```

Before this fix, that leaked block rendered as visible text at the bottom of the page.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing plain redesigns still parse correctly (leading fence stripped as before)
- [x] Documents with a leaked trailing fence now end exactly at `</html>`
- [x] No change to files that already end cleanly

title: fal-redesign: rewrite the redesign prompt to think like a designer
body:
## Summary

The previous system prompt made every redesign look the same — editorial, typography-first, oversized serif, hairline rules, dark canvas. The bias was baked into the rules (e.g. example brand→palette tuples all leaned "editorial photography wants deep ink + warm paper", a hard-ban on cream backgrounds, "do not default to Instrument-Serif-plus-Inter", etc.).

This PR rewrites the rules so the model picks the primary visual carrier — **product-hero image / photography / illustration / typography / diagram / graphic system** — based on the actual brand and content. Illustrated character-led designs for playful brands, type-led designs for slow-media products, photo-led for editorial, etc. The rules no longer default to any one direction.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `scripts/upgrade.sh` on a playful children's / collectibles brand — expect illustrated, character-led output, not serif editorial.
- [ ] Run `scripts/upgrade.sh` on a slow-media / manifesto product — expect typography-first, as before.
- [ ] Run `scripts/upgrade.sh` on a precision-instrument brand — expect product-hero image, possibly photographic.
- [ ] Run `scripts/upgrade.sh` on a B2B SaaS tool — expect clean, trust-forward design without defaulting to the editorial look.

title: Add fal-redesign skill
body:
## Summary

Adds **fal-redesign**, an end-to-end redesign skill for coded websites.

```
your site.html           →  puppeteer screenshot
screenshot + brand       →  opus-4.7 vision writes a redesign prompt
screenshot + prompt      →  fal-ai/gpt-image-2/edit → after.png mockup
after.png                →  opus-4.7 vision writes changes.md + tokens.json
changes.md + original    →  opus-4.7 rewrites the HTML + flux-2 regenerates imagery
before + implemented     →  ffmpeg assembles a split-screen demo MP4
```

Everything runs locally through fal.ai — no browser, no figma, no manual design loop.

## What the PR contains

- `skills/claude.ai/fal-redesign/` — the skill: `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `DEMO.md`, `LICENSE`, 4 scripts, self-contained Node 18+ runtime.
- `skills/claude.ai/fal-redesign/install.sh` — one-command installer (`curl | bash`) that drops the skill into `~/.claude/skills/fal-redesign`.
- `README.md` — fal-redesign row added to the Creative & Production table.

## Models used

- `openrouter/router/vision` with `anthropic/claude-opus-4.7` — VLM#1 (edit prompt) + VLM#2 (build-spec) + implementer.
- `fal-ai/gpt-image-2/edit` — screenshot-to-redesign edit.
- `fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b/edit` — per-tile imagery regeneration for the implemented HTML.

## How to install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fal-ai-community/skills/main/skills/claude.ai/fal-redesign/install.sh | bash
```

Then in Claude Code / Codex:

```
/fal-redesign upgrade ./your-site.html
```

## Demo

25 sites processed end-to-end (20 existing + 5 innovative concepts). Split-screen reel at [video link].

## Test plan

- [ ] `install.sh` runs clean on a fresh macOS / Linux machine with node 18+
- [ ] `bash scripts/upgrade.sh --target ./fixture.html` produces `before.png`, `after.png`, `changes.md`, `tokens.json`
- [ ] `scripts/iterate.sh` produces a valid delta-spec after the agent implements changes
- [ ] `scripts/generate.sh` produces a single-file HTML from a freeform brief

title: fix(fal-scripts): normalize model path for queue request ops
body:
## Background

  In the fal generation scripts, queue request management endpoints (`--status`, `--result`, `--cancel`) should use the **queue-
  level model path**.
  Passing full model paths (for example, `fal-ai/nano-banana-pro/edit` or `fal-ai/kling-video/o3/pro/reference-to-video`) can
  produce mismatched endpoint paths.

  This PR fixes that by normalizing `--model` for these queue operations to the first two path segments.

  ## Changes

  ### 1) `fal-ai-skills/skills/claude.ai/fal-generate/scripts/generate.sh`

  - Added `normalize_request_model()`:
    - `fal-ai/nano-banana-pro/edit` -> `fal-ai/nano-banana-pro`
    - `fal-ai/kling-video/o3/pro/reference-to-video` -> `fal-ai/kling-video`
  - Updated queue operation branches (`--status`, `--result`, `--cancel`) to use normalized `REQUEST_MODEL` in queue API URLs.
  - Kept generation submission behavior unchanged to avoid unintended model behavior changes.

  ## Behavior Impact

  - Affects only queue request management actions:
    - `--status ID`
    - `--result ID`
    - `--cancel ID`
  - Does not change normal generation submission/polling behavior.

  ## Validation

  - `bash -n fal-ai-skills/skills/claude.ai/fal-generate/scripts/generate.sh` passed.
  - Verified queue request URLs now use normalized model path (`$REQUEST_MODEL`) instead of raw `$MODEL`.

  ## Risk / Compatibility

  - Low-risk change.
  - Fully compatible when `--model` is already two segments.
  - Fixes failures for longer model paths by routing queue operations to the correct endpoint.

title: docs: make skill script paths portable via <skills-root>
body:
## What
- Replaced hardcoded `/mnt/skills/user/...` paths in SKILL.md files with portable `<skills-root>/...` placeholders
- Added README note explaining `<skills-root>` replacement

## Why
Hardcoded runtime-specific paths make these skills harder to use outside a specific environment. This keeps docs copy-paste friendly across Claude.ai, Claude Code, and local repos.

## Scope
- Documentation-only change (no script behavior changes)
- Updated 14 skill docs + root README
